# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 16

**1** Jesus said: "Perhaps people think that I have come to cast peace upon the world. They do not know that I have come to cast divisions upon the earth — fire, sword, war.

**2** For there will be five in a house: three will be against two and two against three, father against son and son against father.

**3** And they will stand as solitary ones."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Cast peace... cast divisions"** — the verbal parallel (*nopt* = cast; same as Sayings 9, 10) is essential. Jesus casts fire (Saying 10), the sower casts seed (Saying 9), and here Jesus casts both the false expectation (peace) and the truth (division).

**"Solitary ones" (*monachos*)** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "stand alone." *Monachos* is a technical term in Thomas for the spiritual athlete who has achieved inner unity and stands apart from the social world. PNEUMA's "in the end they will stand alone" makes it sound like isolation; the Coptic implies an achieved state of spiritual singleness.

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- Matt 10:34-36: "I came not to bring peace but a sword" — very close to v.1; Thomas adds "fire" and "war" to the triad
- Luke 12:49-53: Fire and division — combines Saying 10's fire with Saying 16's division; Thomas separates them
- The household division (three against two, two against three) is almost verbatim from Luke 12:52-53

**Thomas-specific:** The addition of *monachos* (v.3) is unique to Thomas and crucial. The division is not the end point; the end point is the solitary one who has passed through division to achieve the singular self.
